description: Cassandra logs shipped by the OpenTelemetry Java agent, on the same label space as the metrics (cassandra_build, host.name, node_role, service_name). Logs and metrics share one time range and one set of variables. NOTE: the log records carry no trace_id or span_id, so there is no trace correlation on this dashboard.

links.title: Log Investigation
links.tooltip: Free-form log search across every service

links.title: Cassandra Overview
links.tooltip: Cassandra metrics for the same time range

panels.title: Volume and severity

panels.description: Log records per interval, split by build and severity. This is what makes log volume comparable between builds. The panel deliberately ignores $severity so the whole mix stays visible; use $severity on the stream and problem panels.

targets.expr: service_name:cassandra "host.name":~"^(${host:pipe})$" cassandra_build:~"^(${build:pipe})$" "scope.name":~"^(${logger:pipe})$" | stats by (cassandra_build, severity) count() as records

panels.title: Log rate by severity and build

panels.description: WARN and ERROR records per interval by build. SEVERE and WARNING are included because the AxonOps and Digitalis agents log through java.util.logging, which uses those names.

targets.expr: service_name:cassandra "host.name":~"^(${host:pipe})$" cassandra_build:~"^(${build:pipe})$" severity:~"^(WARN|WARNING|ERROR|SEVERE)$" | stats by (cassandra_build) count() as problems

panels.title: WARN and ERROR rate by build

panels.description: Loggers ranked by record count over the dashboard time range, with WARN and ERROR counts beside them. Sort any column to re-rank.

targets.expr: service_name:cassandra "host.name":~"^(${host:pipe})$" cassandra_build:~"^(${build:pipe})$" "scope.name":~"^(${logger:pipe})$" | stats by ("scope.name") count() as records, count() if (severity:~"^(WARN|WARNING)$") as warnings, count() if (severity:~"^(ERROR|SEVERE)$") as errors | sort by (records) desc | limit 25

panels.title: Top loggers by volume, with WARN and ERROR counts

panels.description: Which loggers are producing WARN and ERROR over time. A small number of loggers carry almost all of the problem records, so this stays readable.

targets.expr: service_name:cassandra "host.name":~"^(${host:pipe})$" cassandra_build:~"^(${build:pipe})$" "scope.name":~"^(${logger:pipe})$" severity:~"^(WARN|WARNING|ERROR|SEVERE)$" | stats by ("scope.name") count() as records

panels.title: WARN and ERROR rate by logger

panels.description: The agent attaches exception.type, exception.message and exception.stacktrace to records that carry a throwable. This table counts them by type and logger; open a matching line in the stream panel below to read the stack trace.

targets.expr: service_name:cassandra "host.name":~"^(${host:pipe})$" cassandra_build:~"^(${build:pipe})$" "exception.type":* | stats by ("exception.type", "scope.name", cassandra_build) count() as occurrences | sort by (occurrences) desc | limit 20

panels.title: Exceptions by type, logger and build
GCInspector - pause detail the JVM metrics do not carry

panels.description: Duration parsed out of the GCInspector line "<collector> GC in <n>ms", split by build and collector. Read the collector name before you compare: a series named "... Cycles" is a ZGC CONCURRENT phase, not a stop-the-world pause. The branch build logs those because gc_concurrent_phase_log_threshold and gc_concurrent_phase_warn_threshold are enabled on it, so it reports series the stock build never emits. Compare like with like.

targets.expr: service_name:cassandra "host.name":~"^(${host:pipe})$" cassandra_build:~"^(${build:pipe})$" "scope.name":"org.apache.cassandra.service.GCInspector" _msg:"GC in" | extract "<gc_name> GC in <pause_ms>ms" | stats by (cassandra_build, gc_name) max(pause_ms) as max_ms

panels.title: GCInspector reported GC duration, max ms by build and collector

panels.description: How often GCInspector logs at all, by build and collector. GCInspector only logs above its threshold, so this is a count of NOTABLE collections, not of every collection.

targets.expr: service_name:cassandra "host.name":~"^(${host:pipe})$" cassandra_build:~"^(${build:pipe})$" "scope.name":"org.apache.cassandra.service.GCInspector" _msg:"GC in" | extract "<gc_name> GC in <pause_ms>ms" | stats by (cassandra_build, gc_name) count() as events

panels.title: GCInspector events by build and collector
CompactionTask - what compacted, how big, how long

panels.description: Completed compactions per interval, counted from the CompactionTask "Compacted (...)" line. Ground truth against cassandra_compaction_tasks_completed_total.

targets.expr: service_name:cassandra "host.name":~"^(${host:pipe})$" cassandra_build:~"^(${build:pipe})$" "scope.name":"org.apache.cassandra.db.compaction.CompactionTask" _msg:"Compacted (" | stats by (cassandra_build) count() as compactions

panels.title: Compactions completed by build

panels.description: Longest compaction in each interval, parsed from "... in <n>ms.  Read Throughput = ...". Cassandra prints these durations with thousands separators, so the query strips commas before it aggregates.

targets.expr: service_name:cassandra "host.name":~"^(${host:pipe})$" cassandra_build:~"^(${build:pipe})$" "scope.name":"org.apache.cassandra.db.compaction.CompactionTask" _msg:"Compacted (" | extract "in <dur_ms>ms.  Read Throughput" | replace ("," , "") at dur_ms | stats by (cassandra_build) max(dur_ms) as max_ms

panels.title: Compaction duration, max ms by build

panels.description: Mean output size as a percentage of input size, parsed from "(~<n>% of original)". A rising value means compaction is reclaiming less; a falling value means more overwrite or tombstone removal.

targets.expr: service_name:cassandra "host.name":~"^(${host:pipe})$" cassandra_build:~"^(${build:pipe})$" "scope.name":"org.apache.cassandra.db.compaction.CompactionTask" _msg:"Compacted (" | extract "(~<pct_orig>% of original)" | stats by (cassandra_build) avg(pct_orig) as avg_pct

panels.title: Compaction output as percent of original, by build
Dropped messages - the reason, not just the counter

panels.description: Cross-node drops per message type, parsed out of the MessagingMetrics line. cassandra_messages_dropped_total gives the count only; this gives the count split into internal and cross-node, plus the latency below.

targets.expr: service_name:cassandra "host.name":~"^(${host:pipe})$" cassandra_build:~"^(${build:pipe})$" _msg:"messages were dropped" | extract "<mtype> messages were dropped in last <win> ms: <internal> internal and <cross> cross node. Mean internal dropped latency: <int_lat> ms and Mean cross-node dropped latency: <cross_lat> ms" | replace ("," , "") at cross | stats by (mtype) sum(cross) as cross_node_dropped

panels.title: Dropped messages by type, cross-node

panels.description: Internal drops per message type, from the same MessagingMetrics line. An internal drop means the node timed out its own work; a cross-node drop means a peer did.

targets.expr: service_name:cassandra "host.name":~"^(${host:pipe})$" cassandra_build:~"^(${build:pipe})$" _msg:"messages were dropped" | extract "<mtype> messages were dropped in last <win> ms: <internal> internal and <cross> cross node. Mean internal dropped latency: <int_lat> ms and Mean cross-node dropped latency: <cross_lat> ms" | replace ("," , "") at internal | stats by (mtype) sum(internal) as internal_dropped

panels.title: Dropped messages by type, internal

panels.description: Mean cross-node latency of the dropped messages, by type. This is the number the metric cannot give you: how late the message already was when it was thrown away.

targets.expr: service_name:cassandra "host.name":~"^(${host:pipe})$" cassandra_build:~"^(${build:pipe})$" _msg:"messages were dropped" | extract "<mtype> messages were dropped in last <win> ms: <internal> internal and <cross> cross node. Mean internal dropped latency: <int_lat> ms and Mean cross-node dropped latency: <cross_lat> ms" | replace ("," , "") at cross_lat | stats by (mtype) max(cross_lat) as max_cross_node_latency_ms

panels.title: Mean cross-node latency of dropped messages, by type

panels.description: The raw drop lines, so you can read the exact numbers and the node that reported them.

targets.expr: service_name:cassandra "host.name":~"^(${host:pipe})$" cassandra_build:~"^(${build:pipe})$" _msg:"messages were dropped"

panels.title: Dropped message log lines
StatusLogger - Cassandra dumping its own state under pressure

panels.description: How often StatusLogger dumps thread-pool and memtable state, counted from its "Pool Name" header line. Cassandra only does this when it is unhappy, so the firing rate alone is a pressure signal.

targets.expr: service_name:cassandra "host.name":~"^(${host:pipe})$" cassandra_build:~"^(${build:pipe})$" "scope.name":"org.apache.cassandra.utils.StatusLogger" _msg:"Pool Name" | stats by (cassandra_build, "host.name") count() as dumps

panels.title: StatusLogger dumps by build and node

panels.description: Total StatusLogger lines. One dump is many lines, one per pool, table and cache, so this tracks the volume the dumps add to the log.

targets.expr: service_name:cassandra "host.name":~"^(${host:pipe})$" cassandra_build:~"^(${build:pipe})$" "scope.name":"org.apache.cassandra.utils.StatusLogger" | stats by (cassandra_build, "host.name") count() as lines

panels.title: StatusLogger lines by build and node
Correlation - metrics and logs on one timeline

panels.description: Client request latency at ${percentile}, in milliseconds, by build and operation. The metric is emitted in microseconds, so the query divides by 1000 and the panel unit stays short. max by () reports the worst node in each build group, which is correct for any group size.

targets.expr: max by (cassandra_build, cassandra_operation) (cassandra_client_request_latency_${percentile}_microseconds{host_name=~"$host", cassandra_build=~"$build"}) / 1000

panels.title: Client request latency ${percentile} (ms) by build

panels.description: Dropped messages per second from the metric, by type. The > 0 filter removes the ninety-odd verb types that never drop, so only the types that are actually dropping appear. Read this beside the log panels above, which carry the reason.

targets.expr: sum by (message_type) (rate(cassandra_messages_dropped_total{host_name=~"$host", cassandra_build=~"$build"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0

panels.title: Dropped messages rate by type (metric)

panels.description: Stop-the-world GC time as a percentage of wall time, by build. jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles" excludes the ZGC concurrent cycles; without it a ZGC build looks worse than a G1 build, which is backwards.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (cassandra_build, host_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_sum{jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles", host_name=~"$host", cassandra_build=~"$build"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: GC pause overhead, percent of wall time

panels.description: The log lines for the same window as the three metric panels above, filtered by $build, $host, $severity and $logger. Add free LogsQL to the Search box to narrow further, for example: _msg:"timeout". The records carry no trace_id or span_id, so there is no link to Tempo from here.

targets.expr: service_name:cassandra "host.name":~"^(${host:pipe})$" cassandra_build:~"^(${build:pipe})$" severity:~"^(${severity:pipe})$" "scope.name":~"^(${logger:pipe})$" ${search}
